content:
Geometry marks in Class 7 begin here, and the scoring pattern is blunt. Name the angle pair, and the mark takes ten seconds. Fail to name it, and you are guessing. The good news: there are only six pairs to know. Take the free IMO Class 7 Lines and Angles online test below. It has 10 Olympiad-pattern MCQs with instant scoring. Every answer comes with a worked explanation. Aim for 8 out of 10.

What the IMO asks from Lines and Angles in Class 7

  • Complementary and supplementary angles.
  • Adjacent angles, linear pairs and vertically opposite angles.
  • Angles at a point (360°).
  • Parallel lines with a transversal: corresponding, alternate, co-interior.
  • Algebra mixed in: angles as 4x and 5x.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Linear pair sums to 180°; vertically opposite angles are EQUAL.
  • Complement of x is 90° − x; supplement is 180° − x.
  • Parallel lines: alternate angles equal, co-interior angles sum to 180°.
  • If two angles on a line are 4x and 5x, then 9x = 180°, so x = 20°.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Mixing up complementary (90°) and supplementary (180°).
  • Claiming alternate angles are equal WITHOUT parallel lines.
  • Reading vertically opposite pairs off a badly-drawn figure instead of the definition.

questions.q: Two lines are perpendicular to each other. The angle between them measures:
questions.explanation: Perpendicular lines form a right angle by definition. A right angle measures 90°.

questions.q: The measure of an angle is 5 times its complement. The angle is:
questions.explanation: x = 5(90 − x) gives x = 450 − 5x. 6x = 450, so x = 75°.

questions.q: An angle equals one-fourth of its supplement. The angle is:
questions.explanation: x = ¼(180 − x); multiply by 4: 4x = 180 − x. 5x = 180, so x = 36°.

questions.q: The supplement of an angle is 3 times its complement. The angle is:
Ray OC stands on line AB with ∠AOC = (2x − 10)° and ∠BOC = (3x + 20)°. Then x is:
Lines AB and CD intersect at O with ∠AOC = (3x + 15)° and ∠BOD = (5x − 5)°. Then ∠AOC is:
A transversal cuts two parallel lines and one alternate interior angle is 55°. The corresponding angle measures:
questions.explanation: Alternate interior angles are equal, and so are corresponding angles. Both equal 55°.

questions.q: Co-interior angles are in the ratio 2 : 7. The smaller measures:
In triangle ABC, ∠A = 45° and ∠B = 75°. Ray CD meets AB at D with ∠ACD = 20°. Then ∠BCD is:
Ray OS stands on line POQ. Rays OT and OU bisect ∠POS and ∠SOQ. The angle ∠TOU measures:
questions.explanation: Let ∠POS = 2a, ∠SOQ = 2b with 2a + 2b = 180°, so a + b = 90°. ∠TOU = a + b = 90° — the bisectors of a linear pair are always perpendicular.
